Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Body, health & movement

cancer noun

the disease

also tumour, tumor, have cancer, cancerous

classical

Cels. 5.26.31; 6.18.3 (Lewis & Short)
Ov. M. 2.825
Traupman 63, 286
M-O s.v. cancer

cancer, cancrī m.

noun, second declension

a cancer, a malignant growth

In Celsus and Ovid a spreading, eating sore, which the ancients could not cure; Traupman and Morgan–Owens give it for the disease. Its other senses are the crab and the constellation Cancer, and so the summer heat (Ov.). To have cancer: cancrō labōrāre or cancrō afficī (Traupman 64).

Other words

  • carcinōma, carcinōmatis n. — a cancerous sore, a cancer

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cato Agr. 157.4; Cels. 5.28.2; Plin. NH 22.32 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. cancer

    The Greek word, of which cancer is the Latin (Lewis & Short); the medical term.

Examples

  • utque malum lātē solet inmedicābile cancer serpere et inlaesās vitiātīs addere partēs

    and as an incurable cancer spreads far and wide and adds the healthy parts to the diseasedOv. M. 2.825–826

  • Ille cancrō labōrat.

    He has cancer.Traupman 64

See also disease, doctor, treatment, ill.
